title: Bank of America has strong message for Marvell stock investors
detail:
Bank of America has strong message for Marvell stock investors
Moz Farooque
Sun, September 13, 2026 at 1:33 PM EDT 4 min read
MRVL
BAC
NVDA
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Marvell Technology (MRVL) has given its investors plenty to cheer about amid a remarkably choppy AI trade.

Shares of the AI giant have surged over 160% in the past six months, according to Seeking Alpha data, as demand for its data center chips has fueled optimism. According to a note shared with TheStreet, after meeting CEO Matt Murphy and CFO Dan Durn, Bank of America's Vivek Arya sees plenty of reasons to continue doubling down on the stock.

The momentum has continued of late as well. Shares have surged nearly 12% through September 11, while peers like Nvidia (NVDA) shed over 5% in value over the past week.

For perspective, Marvell is involved in building the machinery behind AI. It designs custom processors and the chips that move data between them and allow massive computing systems to work together efficiently.

Its expanded Google partnership, as reported by Yahoo Finance, in particular drew attention, covering chips that support the search giant's AI infrastructure. Also, that agreement grants Google the right to scoop up Marvell shares at a certain price, contingent on future purchases.

But Arya's latest comments, following a management lunch, reach beyond a specific customer.

BofA underscored a growing portfolio of products that could deepen Marvell's role in AI systems. With an October 6 analyst day approaching, investors could soon get an even clearer view of how massive that opportunity could become.

Why BofA is doubling down on Marvell stock

Bank of America has maintained its Buy rating and lofty $365 price target on Marvell stock, implying nearly 55% upside from Marvell's September 11 closing price near $236.10.

More Wall Street:

Wall Street's AI trade faces its biggest valuation test

The next Wall Street shift is already underway

Wall Street sends strong 4-word verdict on the stock market

Analysts led by Vivek Arya base their conviction on how much more technology Marvell could sell within each AI system.

Arya and his team argue that Marvell's biggest opportunity involves supporting the chips that connect processors, manage memory, and move data. That business is a lot harder for customers to replicate than the processors themselves.

Marvell is already shipping these products to the four major U.S. hyperscalers, and each of its custom processors requires one or two supporting chips, which carry a $500 to $1,500 price tag, creating new opportunities for Marvell to earn revenue from its customers as they expand their compute capacity.

BofA estimates this supporting-chip market alone might exceed $60 billion–$65 billion by 2030. At a projected 40%–50% share, Marvell's annual sales opportunity could potentially rise to $30 billion, compared to the management's $3 billion–$4 billion-plus outlook for 2028.

title: A $93 trillion trading boom puts CME in an unusual spot
detail:
A $93 trillion trading boom puts CME in an unusual spot
Faizan Farooque
Sun, September 13, 2026 at 12:03 PM EDT 5 min read
CME
BAC
BTC-USD
Trade CME on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

CME Group (CME) is suing its own regulator over a product that could threaten parts of its futures empire. But Bank of America (BAC) thinks the fight could do surprisingly well for derivatives exchanges, even if CME loses.

The dispute centers on perpetual futures, or perps. Perpetual contracts don't expire, making them easy for traders to leverage exposure without rolling into new contracts.

The product has already launched internationally. Bank of America believes crypto perpetual trading will reach over $93 trillion in 2025, almost five times the size of the underlying crypto spot market.

Now, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) accepted KalshiEX's bitcoin perpetual contract as a futures contract on May 29. The regulator also noted that it should evaluate perpetual products linked to other asset classes on a case-by-case basis.

Less than three weeks later, CME filed suit. Bank of America said CME might do well winning, losing, or just slowing down the regulatory process.

CME lawsuit creates an unusual win-win setup

CME sued the CFTC on June 18 to classify perpetual contracts as swaps, not futures.

This distinction is of considerable commercial importance. If CME wins, perps could be subject to swap-dealer registration, extra reporting requirements, business-conduct rules, and stricter margin standards, according to Bank of America. Such burdens could make it harder to offer the contracts and less attractive to traders.

Related: Billionaire investor makes Amazon his biggest stock bet

But losing might give Bank of America another edge, the bank says. CME has exclusive futures license agreements for key stock indexes such as the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, and Russell 2000. If perps still count as futures, rivals may find it hard to create contracts directly linked to such indices.

Competitors may create their own benchmarks to rival them, but it will not necessarily be simple to lure liquidity away from existing indexes. Regulators might also be forced to reexamine their approval procedure by a procedural court order, holding up new products without firmly deciding whether perps are futures or swaps.

That's why Bank of America says the setup is advantageous for CME in a few situations.

The bank doesn't like the stock overall. This report rates CME Underperform with a $230 price target, compared to its Sept. 10 $274.70 share price. Instead of expecting perps to destroy CME's business, its caution reflects valuation and slower expected earnings growth.

title: 5 reasons to own SMID cap Value
detail:
5 reasons to own SMID cap Value
Navamya Acharya
Sat, September 12, 2026 at 5:49 PM EDT 2 min read
BAC
^RUT
US2000
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- BofA Securities is favoring value stocks over growth in small- and mid-cap equities, citing five reasons including an expected second-half earnings recovery and cheaper valuations.

The Russell 2000 Value is the only size/style index still trading below its long-term average forward price-to-earnings ratio, at 12.5 times versus a 13.3 times average, despite being the top-performing size/style index year to date, BofA equity and quant strategists said.

Mid Cap Value is the least stretched of the remaining indexes at 15.1 times, or 10% above its average.

Growth is historically expensive versus value on four of the six metrics BofA tracks in small caps and in line on the other two, while in mid caps it is expensive on five of six metrics and in line on the sixth.

BofA's five reasons for favoring value over growth in small- and mid-cap (SMID) stocks are an expected second-half earnings-per-share recovery, as value typically leads during profit recoveries; value's outperformance in both mid-cycle regimes and hiking cycles; and less concentration risk, which would benefit if market leadership broadens.

The broker also cites higher quality than growth, with quality expected to lead in the second half. Value is also BofA's favored area within large caps.

Top-ranked sectors in BofA's latest small- and mid-cap quantitative rankings, including real estate and financials in both categories and energy in mid-caps, also have larger weights in the value benchmark than in growth.

Separately, BofA said forward price-to-earnings ratios compressed across small, mid and large caps in August "for good reasons," as positive earnings revisions outpaced price returns. The Russell 2000 forward P/E fell to 15.3 times from 15.7 times, now roughly in line with its historic average of 15.2 times.

BofA's economists have raised their conviction to three rate hikes this year following Federal Reserve official Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and a hawkish jobs report.

A prolonged hiking cycle would pose a key risk for small caps given their leverage and refinancing risk, while higher rates also threaten the manufacturing recovery, since the ISM manufacturing index is negatively correlated with rate changes on a 15-month lag.

The Russell 2000's current P/E is pricing in further ISM deterioration to 52 from the current level of 55.

BofA said it remains constructive on SMID caps versus mega caps given a stronger expected second-half earnings recovery, less-stretched multiples and lower concentration, but sees more upside within SMID for mid caps, which have lagged small caps year to date but carry less risk from Fed rate hikes.

title: CPI Inflation Came Hot: Watch These Stocks If Kevin Warsh Hikes Next Week
detail:
CPI Inflation Came Hot: Watch These Stocks If Kevin Warsh Hikes Next Week
Daragh Thomas
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 3:34 PM EDT 2 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Friday's hotter-than-expected core inflation report has put a Federal Reserve rate hike firmly in play, leaving investors with a more useful question: which stocks could benefit if Chair Kevin Warsh delivers next week? And which might suffer?

Polymarket traders put an 81% chance on a 25-basis-point hike, with about $127 million wagered on the September decision. FedWatch pricing has put the probability around 86.5% after CPI.

Banks Says Higher Rates Help

Bank of America Corp. (NYSE:BAC) may offer one of the clearest positive exposures.

On the bank's July 14 second-quarter earnings call, CFO Alastair Borthwick said its forecast already assumed a 25-basis-point September hike.

"Net, net, we expect that to be a positive," Borthwick said. Bank of America sees 2026 net interest income growth at the upper end of its 6% to 8% range.

Its latest filing shows why: a hypothetical 100-basis-point rise in short-term rates would add about $800 million to net interest income over 12 months, as asset yields rise faster than deposit costs.

Charles Schwab Corp. (NYSE:SCHW) could also benefit from higher short-term rates.

On Schwab's July 21 second-quarter call, CFO Mike Verdeschi said its outlook assumed one hike in December. "If rates resume a hiking pattern you'll see even more expansion," he said, referring to net interest margin.

Schwab expects that margin to reach 3.25% to 3.30% in the fourth quarter, with higher rates increasing what the brokerage earns on client cash and other interest-earning assets.

How Will the AI Trade Fare?

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) is less straightforward.

After Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, Mizuho's Daniel O'Regan said higher-rate expectations historically pressure high-beta technology and long-duration growth stocks.

Bank of America strategist Benjamin Bowler, however, argues the AI boom may withstand substantially higher yields because technology earnings are growing faster than share prices.

That makes Nvidia a key test of whether the old rate-hike playbook still holds. Polymarket traders currently give the AI chip leader a 72% chance of ending 2026 as the world's largest company by market capitalization.

D.R. Horton Faces the Housing Squeeze

D.R. Horton Inc. (NYSE:DHI) sits closer to the other side of the trade.

In its July 21 fiscal third-quarter results, Executive Chairman David Auld said affordability constraints continue to weigh on demand, with sales incentives dependent partly on mortgage rates.

Trading disclosure

RH (RH) faces ongoing margin pressure from higher freight and input costs, which are expected to offset most of the tariff refund benefit while investor focus shifts to the rollout of its Estates offering, BofA Securities said in a Friday note.

BofA noted that RH raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance, with the increase driven entirely by tariff refunds, while higher Vietnam tariffs add further pressure as the country accounts for a significant share of RH's imports.

RH's fiscal Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 12.5% to 13.5% trailed BofA's 19.1% and consensus' 19%, while Q4 revenue growth guidance was 16.1% to 21.2%, with Estates expected to add 8 percentage points, the note said.

BofA said execution of the Q4 outlook and Estates rollout could boost 2027 estimates, while limited housing improvement and higher international startup and preopening expenses of 340 basis points remain concerns.

BofA reiterated its underperform rating on the stock and lowered its price target to $114 from $156.

title: Can Greece Add Another Growth Lever for JPMorgan in Europe?
detail:
Can Greece Add Another Growth Lever for JPMorgan in Europe?
Nikita Kataruka
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 10:09 AM EDT 3 min read
JPM
C
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

JPMorgan's JPM move to expand corporate banking into Greece adds another leg to its broader European growth strategy. By targeting large and mid-sized companies with lending, financing, hedging and investment banking (IB) services, the bank is positioning itself to deepen client relationships and capture a larger share of the corporate wallet.

The expansion also builds on JPMorgan's recent investment in the region, including a 25% increase in global corporate banking staff across Europe, the Middle East and Africa over the past two years, underscoring its focus on gaining scale and market share across EMEA.

The Greece expansion could strengthen JPMorgan's revenue opportunity by widening its corporate client base and creating more scope for cross-selling. Beyond traditional lending, the bank can deepen relationships through treasury, payments, liquidity management, risk solutions and IB services. That broader product mix should help JPMorgan generate both net interest income and fee revenues from the same corporate relationships, supporting more diversified growth over time.

JPMorgan has been building its Greek franchise for several years. In 2022, it announced plans for a new Athens office and a Payments Innovation Lab, initially targeting around 50 hires focused on payments technology, distributed-ledger technology, artificial intelligence and cryptography. The bank's presence in Greece dates back to 1968, and it already provides IB, payments and asset-management services to Greek clients. Separately, JPMorgan consolidated much of its European Union client-facing operations into J.P. Morgan SE in 2022, creating a more scalable structure for serving customers across the region.

For JPMorgan, Greece alone is unlikely to materially impact near-term results, given the bank's enormous global scale. However, the expansion is strategically positive. Adding corporate relationships in a growing economy can support loan balances, payments activity, advisory fees and capital-markets revenues over time, while JPMorgan's existing European infrastructure should provide operating leverage as the business scales.

Expansion Efforts by JPMorgan's Peers

JPM's two close peers, Citigroup C and Bank of America BAC, have also been strengthening their international corporate-banking capabilities in ways that echo JPMorgan's broader EMEA push.

Citigroup continues to lean on its global network to deepen relationships with multinational and institutional clients. In 2025, Citigroup expanded its Token Services platform to Dublin and added euro-denominated transactions, improving 24/7 cross-border liquidity and payment capabilities for corporate clients. More recently, the bank strengthened leadership across its Middle East and Africa franchise, where it operates across 59 markets, reinforcing its focus on cross-border banking, client connectivity and regional growth.

Bank of America has likewise been investing in its global corporate-banking platform, particularly through payments and treasury services. In June 2026, the bank announced plans to launch a cross-border real-time payments solution for corporate, commercial and financial-institution clients, extending the capabilities of its CashPro platform. The effort complements Bank of America's already strong European corporate-banking franchise and could help it capture more payment flows, deepen client engagement and support fee growth.

Bank of America Corp (BAC) analysts said they are more bullish on Cboe Global Markets, CME Group (CME) and Intercontinental Exchange, citing the firms' market positioning and customer bases following disruption from perpetual futures contracts, Bloomberg reported Thursday.

Analysts led by Craig Siegenthaler called Cboe's roughly 30% slump from mid-May to the end of June an "overreaction," pointing to structural advantages in equity options and a professional customer base that reduces the risk of losing business to competing products, the report said.

CME, which is suing US regulators over their approach to perpetual futures, could see a "win-win" outcome regardless of the case's result, Siegenthaler said, according to the report.

A win could slow competitors like Kalshi and Coinbase, while a loss would still let CME rely on its exclusive rights over S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures, the report said.

ICE's franchise is protected by its institutional commodity futures business and its investments in offshore crypto exchange OKX and prediction market Polymarket, which let it "play both sides of the trade," Siegenthaler said, according to the report.

title: BofA stays bullish on a cloud titan that is down 25%
detail:
BofA stays bullish on a cloud titan that is down 25%
Opeyemi Babalola
Mon, September 7, 2026 at 12:33 PM EDT 4 min read
BAC
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Wall Street's two biggest markets are telling opposite stories about the same company right now. Equity investors keep buying every dip. Credit investors keep demanding more insurance against a default that stock buyers barely seem to consider.

Oracle Corporation (ORCL) sits at the center of that disagreement. Shares have fallen 25% since the company's last earnings report, yet BofA Securities is reiterating a Buy rating and a $240 price target ahead of Thursday's fiscal first-quarter results, according to the BofA note shared with TheStreet.

That target implies nearly 65% upside from current levels. BofA bases its $240 target on a 26.5x calendar-year 2027 earnings multiple, a notable premium over the broader software group's 19x average, arguing that rapid backlog conversion justifies the higher price tag.

This is not the first time Oracle's spending has spooked investors. Shares fell 11% in a single session in December 2025 after a smaller capex increase surprised the market, according to Fortune.

The pattern repeated in June 2026, when a bigger than expected capex figure triggered Oracle's steepest one day drop in six months, according to Bloomberg.

Related: BofA names 2 SpaceX alternatives with massive upside

The math behind BofA's confidence

BofA models cloud infrastructure revenue growing 116% year over year this quarter. That would push Oracle's total revenue growth to 28%, up from 21% in the prior quarter, as parts of Oracle's massive contract backlog begin converting into actual sales.

The acceleration matters because it would be the first hard evidence that Oracle's $638 billion backlog, the largest in enterprise software, is turning from promises into cash.

CNBC reported last week that Wall Street holds 42 buy ratings on the stock against just one sell heading into the print, with consensus estimates pointing to similarly steep growth.

Oracle's slower growing software business is quietly holding up too. BofA expects cloud applications revenue to grow 12.8% this quarter, accelerating from 10.3% in the prior period, while the database business keeps expanding into health care and other industry niches, according to the note.

That legacy engine gives Oracle a profitability cushion the AI infrastructure bet does not have on its own.

That growth is not free. BofA expects gross margin to slip to 63.8% and operating margin to 40%, down from 68.7% and 41.8% a year earlier, as the infrastructure business becomes a bigger share of revenue.

Faster growth and thinner margins are arriving together, which is exactly the tension investors are trying to price.
